correctness.rationale: The invariant-cube ODE is cooperative; the stationary scalar root is strictly monotone and has the sharp R=1 crossing. A positive Perron Lyapunov functional plus LaSalle proves critical extinction, and spectral projection yields the exact 1/t critical coefficient for all nonzero states. The allocation is strictly convex and KKT is verified; exact 2-class radical identities and independent optimization/numerical checks succeeded. Residual scope: finite smooth concave classes, deterministic closure; finite tests do not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The examined primary paper treats homogeneous-size mean-field equations and numerical heterogeneous-size settings, rather than the stated finite multi-class nonlinear system with a sharp minimum recovery budget and universal critical coefficient. Paré et al. (2021) have a broader infrastructure network threshold formalism but not the same saturating class equations and joint threshold-cost-asymptotic result; Chen et al. (2017) already derive optimal allocation (the KKT form is acknowledged as known). Literature and research-record comparisons found no exact covering result. A general nonlinear epidemic center-manifold theory might subsume aspects, and uniqueness is not certified by search.
residual_risks: General center-manifold epidemic normal forms might imply the \(t^{-1}\) constant after specialization; no complete bibliographic exhaustiveness is claimed.
The scalar convex recovery budget is a known resource allocation mechanism, not a newly invented general algorithm.
The homogeneous-host class model is a natural extension of the published mean-field equations, not itself an exact heterogeneous finite-hypergraph closure.

value.rationale: The explicit least resource budget for globally suppressing an otherwise endemic aerosol SIS process, together with universal algebraic decay precisely on the budget boundary, answers a motivated intervention cost-versus-time question. Aerosol curvature changes extinction latency even at equal linear threshold. The two-class example has a genuine active-set change and exact radical boundary. Not a mere numerical increment or generic water-filling exercise.
